tool: mcd render: glance-scale visibility and per-job before/after diff
need: Report changed cells and visible-pixel delta per job, render a close-up before/after crop of the target cells, and flag any feature that vanishes or changes nothing at glance distance.
key: mcd render glance scale visibility and per job before after diff
evidence: Rejected chimney: judged 'barely visible at a glance'. Rejected curtains: 'the street view looks the same as before'.
Five rejections say the same thing: the plaque text, the lanterns, the quartz kick-plate, the weathered base and the roof texture are all too small or too sparse to read at a glance.
About 25 'no visible change' observations across jobs (e.g. 'A and B pixel-identical in all four views', 'changes too subtle to read'). Full-size views cannot show 1-block texture.
Most neutral verdicts (plinth, wall field, lintels, sills, chute, wall texture) said the change was too faint to see at full-build scale, so the judge could not assess it.

tool: opening surround: sill, lintel, reveal and drip hood
need: Give openings a recess reveal, a full-width sill or kick-plate, a lintel and a projecting drip hood with a set proud depth, plus an avoid-cells set so trim never cuts pilasters or piers, and enumerate openings per face so zero targets report a blocker.
key: opening surround sill lintel reveal and drip hood
evidence: Rejected 'Fix walkability readout and door reveal': the door-side panel was recoloured to dull grey and brown, which removed colour but did not visibly improve the door reveal at a glance.
'Clean quartz kick-plate under the east gallery windows' was rejected: the strip was a tiny accent that read as a stray bright block, not as a kick-plate.
Drip hoods over every window produced pixel-identical renders, or were too small to see.
Window lintels (front and west flank) and the back door frame showed no change; the back door is not visible in either render, so the job likely had no target.

tool: mcd check: floating, orphan, support and visibility
need: List every block with no face-adjacent support or owning role, fill support under treads and cheeks, and flag detail placements with no exposed face in the standard views.
key: mcd check floating orphan support and visibility
evidence: Stray red cube on the lean-to and detached stone above the gable; both were visible only in the render.
JOB 16 flagpole rod changed no visible pixels in any view
JOB 7 floating finials; JOB 35 stray protruding cornice stubs; JOB 12 stray tan blocks on white piers; JOB 24 stray pale block.
JOB 27: the change opens a see-through hole in the bottom step course and a gap beside the cheek, creating broken voids and a ragged silhouette.

tool: B.pilaster: capital, base and column profile
need: Build a capital and base profile of 1 to 2 blocks for any pilaster, column or post width, so columns read as ornamented shafts instead of plain or slab-like members.
key: b pilaster capital base and column profile
evidence: Entrance sign band end-caps and pillar capitals show no visible change in either build.
'Pilaster capitals and bases (north)' added large flat grey diagonal bands across the white portico and pilasters, which read as artifacts and broke the clean portico.
JOB 9 (pilaster capitals and bases not readable), JOB 12 (portico capitals only a faint lighter band)
JOB 38: arcade posts were only recoloured to a darker, flatter tone with no new profile.

tool: paint vary / weather: contrast floor and clustered coverage
need: Enforce a minimum contrast step and coverage fraction for variation and weathering presets, weathering by contiguous course or panel with clustering rather than scattered single blocks, and a visible default density, including a plinth weathered variant.
key: paint vary weather contrast floor and clustered coverage
evidence: 'Weathered base on the flanks and rear' was rejected: a few mossy and cobble patches were barely visible in either view.

Wall field variation (deepslate, west flank, front) invisible; roof tile variation identical; shaft flank banding and elevator-head banding invisible; chimney texture invisible; deepslate lintels same colour as surround; pier grain only subtle.
Mossy weathered base and plinth weathering/moss invisible; the stepped plinth in one build was the only visible change.
Plinth mossy and cracked variation, wall-field cracked-deepslate patches, shaft-wall and elevator-head stone swaps, oak chute plank patches and wall texture were all judged faint, random speckle.

tool: mcd render: legibility of textures, thin glass, glow and small features
need: Render true textures and opacity, flag untextured or translucent blocks, show a glow halo for light sources, and provide a close-up view so thin glazing and small features are judged, not lost.
key: mcd render legibility of textures thin glass glow and small features
evidence: Rejected task: after-view 'replaces the sandstone bands with translucent pinkish-grey panels that read as glass or a rendering artifact'. The cause is unconfirmed; it may be a block or texture fault rather than a design choice.
Builder: glass_pane is invisible at render scale, so full glass blocks were used instead. Reviewer: glazing reads as small mullioned panes only.
Stained glass rendered pale/pink with no light engine; builder placed shroomlight in the glass to make it read as lit. Reviewer: 'the glowing window is just a small orange patch'.
Weather vane is a thin line hard to see. Cupola almost invisible from front and side views. Slits visible only in the back view. Evidence that the judge cannot see these is inferred, not measured.

tool: mcd palette check: outlier, accent and contrast lint
need: Flag blocks whose luminance, saturation or hue falls outside the build's palette family or breaks their role's contrast, and suggest a contrast-safe substitute per role before render.
key: mcd palette check outlier accent and contrast lint
evidence: Rejected 'Operator touch: clean quartz doorstep': a pure white quartz step is a stark bright patch against mossy grey stone, reading as a mismatched, unweathered tile.
JOB 12 tan blocks on white piers; JOB 24 pale weathered block against dark stone.
JOB 16: gold caps read as odd yellow blocks. JOB 23: cyan soul lantern clashes with the warm lantern palette. JOB 34: bright orange copper cap does not match the dark slate roof.
Builder: 'dark oak fence invisible on dark oak log background'; 'spruce_planks trim invisible on spruce_planks walls'. Reviewer: 'dark roof, dark timber and dark posts merge into one heavy mass'.

tool: sign: spacing, legibility, lettering and fascia clearance
need: Place signs and bands only in solid wall zones above openings, keep clearance from adjacent signs, enforce a minimum readable letter height, and lay out short text as block letters with a plaque fallback.
key: sign spacing legibility lettering and fascia clearance
evidence: Rejected 'Hang a second small sign by the barrel': the dark board butts directly against the READING ROOM sign so the two merge into one long banner, and the dark oak clashes with the lighter board.
Rejected 'Make the sign legible and prominent': sign text unreadably tiny; the fix didn't make it more legible or prominent.
Rejected sign task: new oak beam across the upper storey is a wide plain slab that covers the windows, so the window row looks blocked.
JOB 1 gold lettering read as scattered gold blocks and orange teeth, not legible DEEPSLATE HOLDINGS text

tool: B.lantern: anchored light fixtures
need: Attach lanterns by named feature role (pilaster cap, post top, wall bracket, hung from an overhang) at a size that reads at street scale, through a solid support, aligned to the existing lantern row, and without stray colour cast.
key: b lantern anchored light fixtures
evidence: 'Lamps on the side pilaster caps' was rejected: the lanterns were tiny specks, did not sit on the caps, and the build had no pilaster-cap placement rule.
Portico base lanterns not visible in either render; the job added no discernible detail.
JOB 13: tiny lanterns on a thin dark chain stub, slightly off the pier in the front elevation.

JOB 15: one hanging lantern reads as a stray floating block at the edge. JOB 23: a second bracket and lantern sit on a different level and are offset from the existing lantern, forming a cluttered duplicate pair.

tool: glazing grid: mullions, glazing bars, transoms and panel material
need: Draw mullion and glazing-bar grids in the frame material with set spacing and depth, with a panel-material option for non-glass faces and transom or sidelight variants for doors.
key: glazing grid mullions glazing bars transoms and panel material
evidence: JOB 26 mullion grid is only faintly different from the before state, with flat glass and no crafted depth
JOB 10 glazing change gave flat pale panes with almost no mullion detail
JOB 16: mullion grid shows only faint light-blue lines on the glass.
JOB 17: transom change is tiny and barely shifts the read against the concept's double door.

tool: plaque / signboard: placement on flat, curved, open and lit faces
need: Place one-block sign bands, flanking signs, free-standing or porch-attached signs, and glowing block-letter signs on flat or curved walls.
key: plaque signboard placement on flat curved open and lit faces
evidence: Builder: 'Wall signs... could not fit a 1-cell-high band between awning and viga' and fell back to hand-placed B.sign.
Builder did not build the door sign or pennant because plaque and signboard fail on curved walls.
B.sign gave an unsupported-attachment warning when placed in the wall cell. signboard was not usable because the porch is open on three sides.
Builder: plaque gives flat orange letters; block font needs 5+ rows plus margin. Reviewer (x2): CAFE sign is small, low, hidden by planters, and reads as paint rather than a neon sign.

tool: massing: lean-to, porch, wing and non-rectangular shell
need: Build a lean-to, porch or wing with its own lower roof bonded to the host wall, and a thick-walled shell from any footprint polygon with chamfer or rounded-corner and wall-thickness options, with an orphan check.
key: massing lean to porch wing and non rectangular shell
evidence: Rejected 'Plank/wool lean-to': a patchy strip of wool and plank bands, and a stray red cube sticks out from the side.
Reviewer: 'plain rectangle with one roof mass and no offset wing or porch'; 'add a small projecting entry porch with its own lower roof, or step the eave heights'.
Builder looped over two overlapping rectangles to get rounded corners and a 2-wall shell. Reviewer: 'walls look thin and square-edged, not thick and rounded like adobe'. shell is rectangular only.

tool: B.rail: railing, gate and raised deck
need: Run a single-height railing with regular posts and a continuous top rail round any flat roof, tower top or raised deck, with a gap for steps, a gate prop that reads as an opening between posts, and a footing course under decks.
key: b rail railing gate and raised deck
evidence: Rejected 'Make the garden gate read as a gate': a bare light block with a floating lantern beside the post reads as a stray unfinished pillar, and the open gate, fence and ivy were removed.
JOB 15 tower-top railing: stray pickets, uneven cross-bars, cluttered spiky tangle instead of a clean rail

Builder: 'engawa/veranda all hand-placed'; 'raised floor on footings with 1-block gap: nothing'. Reviewer: 'gaps under the floor show as white or empty holes'; 'flat, uniform plank band with repetitive fence-post railing'.

tool: arch (shapes-curved): openings and heads
need: Apply an arch or segmental head to an existing rectangular opening in place, with an optional stepped or corbelled profile, contrasting voussoir material and keystone.
key: arch shapes curved openings and heads
evidence: JOB 21 arched ground-floor windows show only a darker lintel strip; JOB 32 side door 'stone arch' shows no arch profile; JOB 35 side window lintels barely change
JOB 28 (ground windows show no arched heads), JOB 38 (side door arch shows only a faint grey patch)
JOB 15: corbelled arches over shopfront bays show only as faint stair-step notches in the pale stone.
JOB 19: arch heads over shopfront bays are a small grey block, not the stepped-arch profile. JOB 26: the gold keystone is not visible because no keystone option exists.

tool: relief projection defaults (mcd paint depth)
need: Default projections for sills, pilasters, quoins, cornices, roof trim and crow-steps to at least 2 blocks with a contrasting role material, so 1-block relief does not vanish at street scale.
key: relief projection defaults mcd paint depth
evidence: 'Roof edge' (JOB 11) had only a tiny vent and cap change; 'Roof edge coping' (JOB 10) showed no meaningful roof-edge profile at street view.
JOB 2 pilasters proud of the wall and dark quoins: before and after renders nearly identical; JOB 8 pier capitals and base blocks not visible
JOB 33 stepped dark cap and crenellations are barely visible and do not add the concept's gable stair-stepping
JOB 20 planter ledges, JOB 27 pilasters, JOB 36 eave brackets, JOB 39 coping, JOB 35 cornice: thin, barely visible relief.

tool: thin members: posts, downpipes and pier widening
need: Place posts, rails, downpipes and piers at a minimum 2-wide or capped 1-wide section in a palette role, running continuously from roof edge to ground, widening with the wall's own material and no ragged edges.
key: thin members posts downpipes and pier widening
evidence: JOB 18 handrails are two small sticks; JOB 24 gate posts are thin stubs; JOB 30 post-and-rail strip is barely visible; JOB 31 downpipe became tan posts in the wrong colour
JOB 12: two tan/terracotta blocks at window height, no vertical run; JOB 33: faint mossy strips barely change the read.
JOB 6: widened piers render as pale flat light-oak blocks with a ragged stepped edge on the right pier, clashing with the darker concept tone.

tool: window dressing: shutters and curtains
need: Build closed panel-shaped shutters sized to the opening, outside the glazing, and recess curtains or drapes inside the opening with a depth offset, refusing placement over lanterns, signs or other wall props.
key: window dressing shutters and curtains
evidence: Rejected 'Curtains on the side and back windows': a flat, translucent red strip overlaps the hanging lantern and the wall beside the window, so the back window reads as cluttered.
JOB 31: shutters replaced the glazed window with a black void and thin slats, so the windows read as holes.
JOB 14: the 'shutters' render as two thin vertical brown slats running full window height, so the opening reads as dark and empty.

tool: mcd check: per-face envelope census
need: Report per face the opening count, relief, blank-wall status, and see-through or envelope holes with coordinates, before the render review.
key: mcd check per face envelope census
evidence: Reviewer: 'The back and side walls are flat bands... no openings or relief, so they read as blank'. Current checks did not flag this.
Reviewer saw a see-through hole in the upper tower on the back elevation; mcd check reported orphans but no elevation through-hole finding.
Reviewer: right wall largely open with holes showing interior and sky; front face see-through; back wall has a void. Existing orphan/floating checks did not catch these.

tool: mcd roof: eave overhang, brackets and grow-free overhang
need: Provide an eave overhang with alternating shingle courses and an optional trim line, per-side overhang, overhang kept inside the footprint, and eave brackets that do not need an overhang.
key: mcd roof eave overhang brackets and grow free overhang
evidence: Dark-on-dark deepslate with no courses, texture or eave line. Reviewer asked for alternating deepslate_tile stairs and slabs with a stripped-spruce eave trim.
Builder: overhang on 2 sides only (1 elsewhere); roof() takes one footprint, so the footprint was widened by hand. Reviewer: overhang is shallow and the terrace side is unsheltered.
Overhang grew the grid 15x17x21 to 17x17x22 and shifted coordinates. Builder forced overhang 0, losing the eave. grow:false was too restrictive for a pyramid overhang. Cupola cap went past y=16.
Dark stair corbels under the eave were not possible at overhang 0, because brackets need an overhang to hang under.

tool: B.planter: planter, potted shrub and topiary
need: Place planters and potted shrubs as small volumes of about 3x2 footprint and 2 high, with a leaf or flower palette, at a named bay or corner so they read as planting from the street.
key: b planter planter potted shrub and topiary
evidence: JOB 22 planters are a few tiny dark-green and purple specks, too small to read as shrubs or flower beds
JOB 25 (two thin green strips read as slivers, not potted trees)
JOB 19: potted shrubs and topiary changed no visible pixels in any view.

tool: street dressing: awning, props and stone lantern
need: Place striped awnings attached to the wall or posts at set spacing, clusters of market goods and street props with a grouping option, and a stone lantern with base, post and cap, all sized to read from street distance.
key: street dressing awning props and stone lantern
evidence: Builder: 'stone lantern (toro) hand-built'. Reviewer: 'stone lantern is just one stone post'; 'give the lantern a base, post and cap'.
Builder hand-placed a sloped striped awning in a loop (closest tool is bunting, which is banners only). Reviewer: 'floating awning frame' and 'awning edges ragged where they overlap the viga ends'.
Builder hand-placed decorated_pot, barrel, hay_block and composter. Reviewer: 'clay pots and baskets are small and hard to read at street view'. planter only does window boxes and raised beds.

tool: new: lanternCap (lantern drum with cap, cupola and vane)
need: Build a glazed lantern drum (mullioned glass, iron-bar frame, visible central lamp) with a shallow cap on posts, eave overhang, finial or vane, and a louvred shaft option, sized to a footprint.
key: new lanterncap lantern drum with cap cupola and vane
evidence: Reviewer: the lantern cap reads as a flat black lid or an onion/helmet dome. The roof presets do not cover lantern caps.
Builder hand-placed a ring of glass, iron bars and glowstone. Reviewer: the lantern room is mostly open posts, so the light reads as a small block.
Louvres and shaft hand-built. Cap roof() added layers. No weathervane brush (finial has no arrow, tower top is hollow). Cupola nearly invisible from front; vane a thin line.

tool: timberFrame(g,{rect,y,height,bay,window})
need: Lay half-timber bays with posts, sills, knee or cross bracing, plaster infill, diagonal braces in an X or Z pattern, bargeboards and exposed tie beams for timber gables, with window cut-outs.
key: timberframe g rect y height bay window
evidence: pediment is classical (quartz-style cornice); no timber gable exists. Reviewer asked for symmetrical crossed-beam gable ends with bargeboards.
Timber framing hand-placed. pilasters profile timber is vertical only. Reviewer: stave and St Andrew's crosses wanted.
Plaster, log posts, knee braces and round windows were all hand-looped. Reviewer: 'large flat white panels'. Closest tools (surround timber, pilasters) do not cover bracing or infill.

tool: mcd roof: chimney
need: Place chimneys on the ridge or gable with a flue and cap, measure rise from the local roof surface, optionally band the stack with a flared cap, and flag a floating stub.
key: mcd roof chimney
evidence: Chimney was a 2x2 with no flue or top. Reviewer: a floating chimney stub and a grey stone stub beside the tower.
rise is relative to the roof apex, so a chimney at the eave towered over the roof; a negative rise was needed. Reviewer: 'chimney floats beside the roof with a visible gap', 'stuck on'.
Reviewer: chimneys are short, plain and flat-topped. Builder: 'roof --chimney can only sit on a roof, not rise from a wall plane'; hand-built caps.

tool: plinth <F>: base treatment and approach steps
need: Break a large blank base with a stair course, cobble/mossy mix and plinth step, add a half or full approach course centred on a chosen face, and default a continuous plinth to the full footprint.
key: plinth f base treatment and approach steps
evidence: Stone base large, blank and flat. plinth <F> exists in detailing.md but was not used; builder left the base blank. Reviewer wants a stair/slab course and a cobble/mossy mix.
Builder: entry steps on the plinth placed by hand; no steps brush for plinths.
Reviewer: loose stone stubs at the base; asked for a continuous stone plinth. Builder had orphan and floating cleanup but not a base plinth.

tool: mcd roof: chimney seating and replace mode
need: Chimneys seat on the local roof plane down to the sloped surface under their footprint, take a dark masonry cap by default, and offer a replace mode that removes the old stack.
key: mcd roof chimney seating and replace mode
evidence: Rejected 'Chimney on the west gable': a single bright pale cap sunk into the dark slate reads as a light patch or hole, not a stack, and is barely visible at a glance.
JOB 17 flat-topped light-grey column clashes with deepslate and its cap is stuck to a stray roof fragment
JOB 34: the new chimney is a wide detached block floating off the roof slope with a visible gap beneath, and the old thin chimney is still standing beside it.

tool: projecting band: string course, cornice and dentils
need: Offer a continuous string course or cornice that projects at least 2 blocks, runs between storeys on every face, uses a dentil or corbel rhythm, and returns cleanly at corners with no detached stubs.
key: projecting band string course cornice and dentils
evidence: Mid string course between storeys not visible in either render; shaft flank storey bands add no visible profile.
JOB 7 (eave ledge nearly invisible), JOB 8 (belt courses faint), JOB 10 (roof coping barely visible), JOB 12 (heavy dentilled cornice and string course not produced)
JOB 35 cornice shows stray stubs at the sides; JOB 36 eave brackets barely visible; JOB 34 dentil row changed no pixels.

tool: mcd check: orphan and support rules
need: Run floating-block and orphan checks as a gate on the exported build, on all faces, accept sea_lantern and role-declared intentional orphans, and flag unsupported finials.
key: mcd check orphan and support rules
evidence: Reviewer: floating grey slab fragments hang beside the tower and the rear of the cottage has stray blocks. The build passed a check run on an earlier version.
Builder: sea_lantern flagged as an unsupported lantern by check; palette flags glowstone downlights as outliers.
check flags hanging bale, pyramid cap top and interior shroomlight as orphans, all intended. A floating spire finial was not caught.

tool: facade rhythm: all faces, pilasters and bands
need: Apply window slits, pilasters at every n blocks, and regular metal bands with rivet panels to every face, without growing the grid.
key: facade rhythm all faces pilasters and bands
evidence: Reviewer: 'the rear stone shaft is a blank wall with only a couple of odd blocks', 'add a window slit, buttress or ivy streaks and a lantern on the back stone shaft'.
Reviewer: copper accent patches on brick walls are random and unframed; wants ordered horizontal bands or riveted panels at regular spacing.
pilasters every n profile timber grew the grid, so board-and-batten posts were hand-placed on a rhythm.

tool: lantern fixture: hanging under eaves, with material option
need: Hang lanterns from a chain or bracket under any eave, overhang or beam underside, spaced evenly, with copper, iron or spruce material chosen by option.
key: lantern fixture hanging under eaves with material option
evidence: Builder: lanterns on chains placed without support. Reviewer: lanterns float without visible support in the back view and look loose.
Builder: 'fixtures at eaves only works on facades found by face maps and could not reach the jetty corners'. Reviewer: 'lanterns are sparse and hang on odd chains'.
Builder: hanging lantern in fixture defaults to spruce/iron; had to hand-place copper_lantern.

tool: B.finial / B.flagpole: vertical element on apex or roof point
need: Place a grounded pole with an optional cap or ball on any apex, roof corner or pediment foot, scaled so it reads as a finial or flagpole, with no air gap and a finial material drawn from the palette role.
key: b finial b flagpole vertical element on apex or roof point
evidence: JOB 12 finial is an orange-red ball on a thin stalk, clashing with the slate and gold palette; concept has slender gold spires
JOB 14 (pediment finial too small), JOB 17 (tower flagpole one block), JOB 24 (lantern posts at plinth ends unreadable)
JOB 7: thin stone rods float at roof corners and pediment feet, reading as antennae with some hovering off the eave.

tool: glazing grid (brush option, applied to gables and new bays)
need: Apply glazing and louvre grids inside gable triangles, on belfry walls and on new bays, with floor-to-ceiling mode, pane-to-pier ratio, and a curtain-wall bay rhythm on any face.
key: glazing grid brush option applied to gables and new bays
evidence: glazing grid works on flat facades but not inside gable triangles. Builder hand-placed lattice windows; reviewer wanted a louvred belfry in place of the see-through hole.
Builder: no curtain-wall brush; posts placed by hand. Reviewer (x2): brief's floor-to-ceiling glass not visible; glass shows only as small panes between black piers; side and back walls blank.
Builder: glazing brush works on existing walls only. Reviewer: back and side walls remain blank planes.

tool: mcd render: interior and eye-level views
need: Include an interior or through-window view in the default view set whenever a job touches interiors, so changes not visible from outside can be judged.
key: mcd render interior and eye level views
evidence: Rejected 'Interior stock and meeting room': the changes are barely visible from outside, so the judge cannot see the work.
JOB 22 interior furnishings invisible in exterior views; JOB 24 one-block paving change and JOB 25 moss flecks too small to judge.

tool: mcd render: true colour and entity visibility
need: Render white and paper blocks at true luminance and show banners and entity blocks in the standard close-ups, or state explicitly that they are not rendered.
key: mcd render true colour and entity visibility
evidence: JOB 11: teal corner banners do not appear in front or front-left close-ups; only a tan block change shows.
Builder: 'paper white renders light grey in mcd render (white concrete / wool)'; snow_block was the only clean white. Reviewer: 'paper-screen walls barely read'.

tool: palette by role: role-to-block mapping
need: Map roles such as wall, post, corner, roof, white/quartz and accent gold to architectural blocks by contrast with the wall role, and reject non-architectural blocks like wool as facade or roof material unless marked decorative.
key: palette by role role to block mapping
evidence: Rejected stepped-peak task: stripped log corner posts clash with the dark stone walls, so the roofline looks less crafted.
Rejected lean-to: red and yellow wool blocks read as clutter on a building facade.
JOB 27 quartz cap and bands read as a mismatched thin grey strip instead of white quartz

tool: coping and parapet: continuous top-edge course
need: Build a single continuous coping course around the full wall-top ring by default, with a separate coping material and per-side railing or parapet options, failing the job if the ring is not closed.
key: coping and parapet continuous top edge course
evidence: Roof-edge coping left stray specks on the rooftop with no edge improvement; roof-line coping on the front frieze not visible.

Builder used paint railing rules with explicit x ranges because roof had no per-side railing or coping option. Reviewer: 'fence posts poke above the parapet'. Also 'deck's mud-brick slab merges with the coping'.
Reviewer: 'the parapet is thin and patchy, with the crenellation present on only some sides' and 'a continuous slab or wall parapet around the whole roof edge'.

tool: new: ring brush (corbel course and arcade)
need: Build a ring of upside-down stair or slab corbels with per-cell facing, or an arcade of evenly spaced posts with rail or lattice, a gap to the inner wall, and a beam line.
key: new ring brush corbel course and arcade
evidence: Builder hand-placed a corbelled gallery under a round tower with jagged diagonals. Reviewer: the gallery floor and cap stack into a dark slab.
Gallery (svalgang) ring built by hand around the core. Reviewer: evenly spaced plank pillars read as a warehouse wall; wants an open arcade with a gap to the inner wall and a base plinth.

tool: landscaping: mound and rock outcrop plinth
need: Build a height-field mound or rock outcrop with a cut-in stepped stair, moss and fern cover, and one cobble/moss mix, sized for small plinths.
key: landscaping mound and rock outcrop plinth
evidence: Builder hand-wrote a height loop for a rocky outcrop. heightfield and strata are for valleys, not rock islands.
Hand-written height-field loop. Reviewer: 'stone base platform is noisy and irregular', 'base has scattered grass and moss blocks'. Landscaping brushes did not fit a tiny plinth.

tool: mcd roof: tall spire and cone profiles
need: Provide proportionate steep pitch for small footprints, a flared-base broach spire, and a smooth tall cone with per-ring lean and taper, without stair-step lumps.
key: mcd roof tall spire and cone profiles
evidence: steep pyramid on a 3x3 belfry gave a thin needle. Reviewer: spire and cross finial are small; wants a tall slender shingled needle.
Builder wanted a broach option on tower: spire; pyramid gave a straight needle with no flare at the base.

Pyramid is a square-stepped, centred, broad form; reviewer wanted 'a tall crooked wizard's cone', 'lean barely visible'. A rejected cone attempt read as 'a tall ragged green mass with irregular stair-step protrusions'.

tool: new: hoist (jib, crane beam and hoist beam)
need: Build a beam projecting past a wall or gable with a bracket, hanging chain, hook and load, sized relative to the opening below.
key: new hoist jib crane beam and hoist beam
evidence: Reviewer: crane arm and hoist not legible, nothing above the loading door. Builder: 'Crane / gantry / jib: nothing.'
Logs, stair bracket, iron_chain and hay bale all placed by hand. Closest existing tool is attach lantern. Bale flagged as orphan.

tool: props: prop groups and free-standing props
need: Scatter prop groups (bales, barrels) and free-standing props such as a telescope on a stand, plus a fence-run brush that works on grade and stops at path gaps.
key: props prop groups and free standing props
evidence: No prop library; closest was lightning_rod + fence. Rejected task: 'telescope is now a black slab that floats past the wall with no visible support'.
Bale stacks, barrels and fence with path gap all hand-placed. planters covers only windows and beds. railing works on a roof top, not on grass.

tool: B.plaque: raised-panel inscription tablet
need: Place a raised-panel tablet with legible inset lettering and gold-trim or gold-leaf frame option, keeping clearance from posts and signs.
key: b plaque raised panel inscription tablet
evidence: 'Make the name plaque legible and gold' was rejected: the text was unreadable and the plaque was not visibly gold.
JOB 3 INSPECTORATE plaque: raised carved panels became flat pale stone plus dark blocks and a wood post cutting the sign band; reads patchy, not a plaque.

tool: gable edge: raking band and apex cap
need: Build a continuous stair-stepped raking band that follows the pitch on both gable edges, plus a stepped apex cap bonded to the roof and wall cells beneath it.
key: gable edge raking band and apex cap
evidence: Rejected 'Stepped stone peak above the gable': a boxy, detached stone lump floats above the gable with a visible hole beside it.

tool: gable tympanum: emblem inlay and pattern fill
